[RFCS.6.9] **How the engine numbers its facts.** The engine must give each
fact its `fact_id` from one counter per engine, which starts at 1 and
increases by 1 with each id taken. The engine takes the next id:

- for each fact that enters working memory, whatever put it there: a host
  assert, a rule's `emit`, an `ExternalAssert` delivery, in [RFCS.24.3]'s
  order, a hydrated row ([NCBK.9.3]) or a fault fact ([LERR.9.8]). An
  identity update's replacement is a fact that enters ([RFCS.6.7]);
- for each host assert a bound refuses, whose `FactAssert` is recorded
  although no fact enters ([RFCS.6.7]). No later atom names that id.

The engine takes no id for a no-op reassertion, whose `FactAssert` carries the
live fact's id ([RFCS.6.7]), nor for a host call refused as not a well-formed
input, which records nothing, nor for a fact the lowering or the engine
creates for its own use ([RFCS.6a.5], [LDET.5.8]). No fact has the id 0, so a
`fact_id` field holding 0 names no fact. A clone continues the counter
([IARC.11.2]).

The ids are observable. Every compared body carries them ([RFCS.6a.3]), so a
replay matches its recording only if it numbers as the recorded run did.
